devops-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Elevated 5xx rate detected on text-gen-stage canary (service=text-gen, route=/v1/generate). Error rate 18% over 3m. Canary ID=canary-2026-03-17-42.
sophia: seeing same in Grafana, spikes start ~2m after deploy. canary only.
ajay: any deploy metadata? which image/tag rolled?
devops-bot: Deploy metadata: pipeline=ci/cd-pipeline-9, image=text-gen:staging-20260317-87, previous=image=text-gen:staging-20260316-44. No manifest mismatch flagged by CI.
marcus: 503s and some 502s in EU region primarily. Customers hitting the route get 503s intermittently. CS Erin, any reports?
cs-erin: we have 2 small customers in EU reporting failed generates since ~09:12UTC, both low traffic. I'll open a support ticket and flag impact low->medium if more reports come.
sophia: digging into pod logs now, seeing repeated error: "kv-cache: unexpected token in manifest" and "model load failed: model files checksum mismatch"
ajay: checksum mismatch smells like image/manifest mismatch or stale layer pulled from registry cache. Could be mutable tag drift. Did pipeline use a mutable "staging-latest" anywhere?
ops-lead: @ajay good call. Pager: if this is a bad artifact, prefer rollback/killswitch. We should stop canary traffic immediately and rollback canary to yesterday's image.
marcus: agree. Can we flip routing for canary to fallback model? We have a feature-flag to route canary -> stable-model. Can someone flip it?
sophia: flipping flag in FeatureGate:service/text-gen -> set canary_route=false now.
sophia: :white_check_mark: FeatureGate updated, canary traffic should route to stable. Monitoring...
devops-bot: Routing change observed. Error rate on canary group dropping to baseline within 30s.
ajay: still want to revert the broken deploy to avoid future drift. Running rollback now:
```
ci deploy rollback --pipeline ci/cd-pipeline-9 --to-job ci/cd-pipeline-8
```
marcus: rolling back via k8s as well to be safe:
```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/text-gen --to-revision=44
```
ops-lead: hold on on k8s undo until CI rollback completes, avoid conflicting rollouts. Watch deployment status.
sophia: CI rollback finished, image now text-gen:staging-20260316-44. Watching pods.
marcus: pods are stabilizing, readiness probes passing. 503 rate back to normal.
cs-erin: notified affected customers with ETA for fix and asked them to retry. I'll follow up if more reports come.
ajay: after rollback, I pulled manifests from registry and compared checksums: staging-20260317-87 manifest references a layer digest that wasn't present in the mirror cache (mirror returned 404 then 200 with older digest). Likely registry propagation/inconsistent retag during the build window.
sophia: will open a postmortem ticket for CI publish->registry propagation edge case. Also adding a guard: require immutable digest pin in pipeline for canary deploys.
ops-lead: agreed. Immediate mitigation checklist: feature-flag fallback (done), CI rollback (done), monitoring & CS notified (done). Assigning incident owner: marcus. Marcus, you're oncall lead for this incident.
marcus: taking over incident. I'll coordinate postmortem with infra and CI owners. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
sophia: leaving notes in the deploy pipeline run and tagging pipeline owner @ci-team.
devops-bot: Incident closed: canary spike mitigated, root cause suspected: registry retag/propagation causing stale/mismatch layer fetch for new image. Next: postmortem + pipeline guard.
marcus: filing a follow-up doc and adding runbook step to block mutable tags in canary pipelines.
cs-erin: follow-up: customers updated; will close tickets after confirmation.
ops-lead: nice quick mitigation. Keep timeline and logs in the incident ticket. :hand:
